adversarial_review.check: All statements are restricted to the ten registered dimensions and three beta values; endpoint ratios and maxima are diagnostics, not limits.
Signs are retained only within the exact union-support group and absolute pair aggregates are reported separately.
The reversed term order is rebuilt in each lane and compared with the negative forward group; residuals pass the declared tolerance.
rho_U is the normalized finite induced two-site Gibbs matrix and is not identified with an infinite-volume KMS restriction.
Each of the four K_U^(1/2)-Gibbs legs is computed separately, with no spectral commutation assumed.
Only the fixed source edge {0,1} and declared finite oscillator matrices are used; no external bond or exact untruncated CCR is inserted.
The independent lane reconstructs oscillator, support terms, Gibbs/energy factors and signed groups without importing the primary module.
Common core, cutoff removal, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
R358 checks exact dimensions, beta/source counts, rational slope arithmetic and scope only; matrix spectra and QFT limits remain Python/open analysis.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite high-cutoff signed-cancellation stress on a fixed two-site graph. It is not an asymptotic divergence theorem, global no-go, common-core construction, thermodynamic dynamics, OS/KMS/GNS result, mass-gap proof, continuum result, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or Clay closure.
decision_reason: The high-cutoff extension confirms that exact union-support sign grouping does not by itself stabilize the energy-weighted history coefficient. The coefficient fluctuates with truncation and beta but remains finite-grid growing relative to d=3, while signed cancellation leaves roughly 71-83 percent of the absolute endpoint aggregate. This is enough to reject this finite signed-group coefficient as an unqualified common-core input. The result is route-local: it does not decide a cancellation kernel with additional spectral/state weights, nor does it establish untruncated divergence.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 134/134 assertions over 30 high-cutoff beta rows. The integrated verifier passes 1381/1381 and Lean R358 compiles. Reverse-order residuals are zero on this finite matrix fixture. The signed energy-weighted per-site coefficient is nonmonotone but reaches 38.01539989463614 at d=20,beta=0.5 and 8.670037823582929 at d=10,beta=1; the d=24/d=3 endpoint ratios are 27.178403353918984 (beta=0.5), 2.732285890441825 (beta=1) and 1.390589686602203 (beta=2). Signed-to-absolute endpoint ratios remain 0.7092101515841736, 0.7739775356170933 and 0.8276235228192911, so cancellation is substantial but incomplete. The finite maxima and endpoint growth do not supply a cutoff-, beta- or global-state-uniform coefficient.
method: Hold the exact two-site Q3 edge and source support {0,1} fixed while sweeping oscillator dimensions d in {3,4,5,6,8,10,12,16,20,24}.
For each d and beta in {0.5,1,2}, rebuild the local induced Hamiltonian, Gibbs matrix, positive shifted energy and every overlapping signed union group.
Compare the signed union-group raw, two-sided Gibbs and K^(1/2)-Gibbs seminorms with the corresponding absolute pair aggregates and explicitly reverse the term order.
Reconstruct the same table in an independent implementation and cross-check finite counts, exact fixture arithmetic and the scope firewall in Lean R358.
next_action: Seek a genuinely state-compatible cancellation kernel or spectral-window history estimate, with an analytic cutoff-uniform bound on a declared common core; do not promote the finite signed-group coefficient or common alpha until that proof is supplied.
no_overclaim: Finite high-cutoff signed cancellation remains a route-local diagnostic. It neither proves nor disproves an untruncated Q3 limit, global KMS state, common core, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.

qft_interface.closed: A reproducible high-cutoff two-site signed-union table with reverse-order antisymmetry and local Gibbs/energy-weighted diagnostics across three beta values.
qft_interface.open: A cutoff-uniform global-state-compatible cancellation estimate, common core, actual Trotter defect, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

question: Does exact union-support sign cancellation remain cutoff-stable on the fixed two-site source edge under high oscillator dimensions and local Gibbs/energy weights?
title: Finite Q3 high-cutoff signed cancellation audit
